ui.overviewDescription: Locations, orientations, and distances use OpenStreetMap coordinates at 1:1 scale and were cross-checked against Isha’s 2026 campus map. Buildings are modeled from official and visitor photographs. Adiyogi is to the southeast and faces south. The Velliangiri Hills are to the west. Use Cutaway to look inside buildings.
ui.outTip: Show only the buildings outside Sarpa Vasal.
ui.inTip: Show only the buildings inside Sarpa Vasal.

adiyogi.name: Adiyogi statue
adiyogi.description: A steel bust of Shiva, 34 meters tall and 45 meters wide, faces due south as Dakshinamurti. It stands about 840 meters southeast of the main campus. Inside the square pavilion in front, the silver Yogeshwar Linga sits in a dark circular basin. The pavilion has a terracotta roof and a six-pointed star inlaid in its floor.

yogeshwar.name: Yogeshwar Linga
yogeshwar.description: The linga in front of Adiyogi represents five major chakras. Visitors can offer water and neem leaves and walk around it.

kalabhairava.name: Kalabhairava
kalabhairava.description: This black-painted stone shrine stands west of Adi Yogi Isha Road, between Adiyogi and Malai Vasal. Tall, narrow windows line the side wall. Carved columns support a copper-toned fascia beneath a dark figure of Kalabhairava. A low stone wall and black iron railing border the paved forecourt.

kalabhairava-in.name: Kalabhairava interior
kalabhairava-in.description: A dark boulder with a narrow vermilion mark rests on a rough stone base. Red flame shapes are attached to the black cords hanging just behind it. There is room to walk or sit around the rock and behind the cords.

malai.name: Malai Vasal main entrance
malai.description: The main entrance sits on Adi Yogi Isha Road, about one kilometer south of Adiyogi. The road passes beneath a natural boulder that rests on two stone pillars and supports a small black linga. Inside the open wooden gates, a pond with frangipani trees lies to the west.

sarpa.name: Sarpa Vasal gate
sarpa.description: This campus entrance on Narasipuram Road has stepped granite frames, red brick trim, a terracotta-colored arch, and a black cobra in the gateway. The Information Center is just inside. Stalls and Surya Vasal lie along the road to the northeast.

moondram.name: Moondram Pirai Eatery
moondram.description: The restaurant sits across the road south of Sarpa Vasal, next to an ATM. The model uses the site footprint from OpenStreetMap and visitor photographs for the interior. The exterior is an approximation. Use Cutaway to see inside.

moondram-in.name: Restaurant interior
moondram-in.description: The interior has white walls, white steel roof trusses, pale floor tiles, and four-seat iron tables. A Devi image hangs on the east wall. Visitor photographs show cone-shaped dosas and baby corn. The other food in the model is illustrative.

roadside-food.name: Roadside food stalls
roadside-food.description: Small food stalls line the right side of the road as you walk from Moondram Pirai toward Adiyogi. The stalls are shown in approximate locations.

c-section.name: C Section
c-section.description: Partway to Adiyogi, three rows of food stalls form a square-cornered C around an open courtyard. The tour shows the approximate location and layout.

neem-point.name: Neem Point
neem-point.description: This food stop is near the large parking lot on the road from Adiyogi to Malai Vasal. The stalls are shown in an approximate location.

adiyogi-parking.name: Adiyogi parking
adiyogi-parking.description: A large surface lot near Neem Point serves visitors arriving at Adiyogi from the Malai Vasal side. The parked cars and motorbikes are illustrative.

unavagam.name: Velliangiri Unavagam
unavagam.description: A South Indian vegetarian restaurant southeast of Suryakund and just inside Surya Vasal. Stainless-steel serving windows line the mustard-yellow kitchen building behind an open shelter with rows of standing tables. The small Isha Life shop at the east end is shown in an approximate location.

unavagam-in.name: Under the dining shelter
unavagam-in.description: Diners queue at the serving windows and eat at long standing tables under steel frames, a metal roof, and ceiling fans. A small Isha Life shop has a glass storefront at the east end.

suryakund.name: Suryakund and Mandapam
suryakund.description: The men's bathing pool lies 22 feet below ground, surrounded by the columned Suryakund Mandapam. The 28 broad eastern steps lead to a pool 130 feet long and 40 feet wide. A 20-foot copper sun hangs beneath a brick arch. The steps are used for early morning Guru Pooja and practice. Use Cutaway to see inside.

surya-in.name: Steps and pool
surya-in.description: From the landing by Naga Shrine, look down over the broad stone steps and practice mats. Two tall stone columns stand partway down. The bottom steps descend into the water, and a curtain of water runs down the opposite wall.

naga.name: Naga Shrine
naga.description: At the head of the eastern Suryakund steps, intertwined cobras are carved into a single black stone. Brass lamps and vessels holding green leaves stand in front. Use Cutaway for a clearer view beneath the roof.

ponds.name: Lotus ponds and arched bridge
ponds.description: A white arched bridge crosses the narrow part of the gourd-shaped lotus ponds between Nandi and Suryakund. The bridge is on the walking route from Dhyanalinga to Suryakund.

nandi.name: Nandi
nandi.description: The reclining black bull, about 15 feet tall, faces Dhyanalinga. It has a raised head, a prominent shoulder hump, crescent-shaped horns, and a string of bronze bells. One folded foreleg rests on the ground as if the bull is about to rise.

dhyanalinga.name: Dhyanalinga
dhyanalinga.description: Completed in 1999, Dhyanalinga has an ochre brick dome 76 feet across and 33 feet high. The stone base has 28 triangular vents. From the east, visitors pass the Pillar of Religions, a stone gate, steps, reliefs, and the figures of Patanjali and Vanashree before entering through a stone archway.

dhyana-in.name: Inside Dhyanalinga
dhyana-in.description: The black granite Dhyanalinga stands 13 feet 9 inches tall. Seven copper bands mark the seven chakras. Coiled serpents form its pedestal, surrounded by the square jalaseema pool. There are 28 meditation niches around the wall and a gold-plated copper hemisphere suspended overhead that drips water.

bhairavi.name: Linga Bhairavi
bhairavi.description: The Devi shrine, consecrated in 2010, stands southwest of Dhyanalinga. The walls form an inverted triangle symbolizing a womb, with a smaller triangular sanctum at the far end. The roof has a triangular skylight. Use Cutaway to see inside.

lb-in.name: Devi and the trident
lb-in.description: A large trident stands at an angle in the hall. Four steps descend toward the sanctum, bordered by brass posts and red ropes. The eight-foot Devi has three eyes and ten arms and wears a red and gold sari. Carved white columns and oil lamps flank the shrine. The Devi Office and Ritual Office are next door on the ground floor of Sadhana Hall.

sadhana.name: Sadhana Halls 1 and 2
sadhana.description: This two-story building west of Dhyanalinga has ground-floor rooms along a colonnade, including the Devi and Ritual offices at the south end. Upstairs, Hall 1 is to the north and hosts daily Darshan, Aumkar initiation, and early morning practices for women. Hall 2 is to the south. The ground-floor layout is approximate.

chandrakund.name: Chandrakund
chandrakund.description: The women's bathing pool sits just north of Dhyanalinga. Two stone turtles stand by the entrance, where a red-brick arch meets a steel canopy. Thirty-two stone steps descend about 30 feet to the pool and a Kerala-style mural depicting the Mahakumbha Mela.

chandra-in.name: Steps down to the pool
chandra-in.description: Thirty-two stone steps lead between boulder walls to the pool and its linga, about nine meters below ground. The vault overhead carries the Mahakumbha Mela mural.

deposit.name: Deposit counter
deposit.description: Visitors can leave phones and luggage here before entering the campus. The counter appears with a phone icon northeast of Chandrakund on the official map. The appearance of the building is approximate.

ishalife.name: Isha Life and Peppervine Eatery
ishalife.description: Open-front Isha Life shops line the west side of the main road with shelves, display stands, and clothes racks. Their exteriors are approximate. To the northwest, Peppervine Eatery has carved stone columns, a steel-truss canopy, and stone water troughs with water lilies.

welcome.name: Welcome Point
welcome.description: Visitors register here, meet volunteers, and can access phones and internet. Shuttles and bullock carts depart from here. The carts go to Metal Bridge near Bhiksha Hall. Numbered registration counters sit behind bamboo screens under dark tiled roofs, and a covered pickup area stands by the road.

spanda.name: Spanda Hall
spanda.description: The roughly 64,000-square-foot hall hosts advanced programs such as Bhava Spandana. It has an ochre plinth, square stone columns, and a low metal roof with a skylight. The earthen-walled front garden has a large lawn, three pavilions, and a stone-edged lotus pond. Use Cutaway to see inside.

spanda-in.name: Inside Spanda Hall
spanda-in.description: The hall has white marble floors and a stepped coffered ceiling with rows of lights. The north wall holds a 140-by-12-foot Kerala-style mural of Adiyogi's life, painted with plant and mineral pigments. A stone dais stands in front of it.

alayam.name: Adiyogi Alayam
alayam.description: This roughly 82,000-square-foot hall just north of Suryakund has an open front, a low pale-pink arched roof, and stone columns carved with serpents. The main interior is column-free.

nalanda.name: Nalanda
nalanda.description: To the north, Nalanda Stay is a white three-story lodging and conference building with an open hall beneath a curved roof between its wings. The large Nalanda Grounds to the south are used for evening games.

bhiksha.name: Bhiksha Hall
bhiksha.description: In the dining hall at the north of the campus, about two thousand people can sit in rows on the floor and eat in silence. The south side has an entrance porch and washbasins. The exterior model is simplified. Use Cutaway to see inside.

metalbridge.name: Metal Bridge
metalbridge.description: This steel-truss footbridge northeast of Bhiksha Hall crosses a mountain stream toward Velliangiri Prashala. It is the final stop on the bullock cart route from Welcome Point. The bridge location and the stream’s route from the Velliangiri foothills through campus are approximate.
